analysis.evidence: הַפָּלִיט names the one who came. The next clause, וַיַּגֵּד לְאַבְרָם, recounts what the fugitive did upon arrival: he told Abram.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with הַפָּלִיט, “the fugitive.”

analysis.evidence: The same man is the subject of וַיָּבֹא (“he came”) and וַיַּגֵּד (“he told”). The narrator identifies him by his escape as he brings news to Abram.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: The escapee is the subject of both וַיָּבֹא (“he came”) and וַיַּגֵּד (“he told”). The following לְאַבְרָם identifies Abram as the recipient of the news.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with הַפָּלִיט, the escapee.
analysis.sense: tell someone that something is the case

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּגֵּד לְאַבְרָם הָעִבְרִי, the fugitive reports to Abram, whom the verse identifies as “the Hebrew.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks Abram, a masculine personal name, as the recipient of the report.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: In לְאַבְרָם הָעִבְרִי, the fugitive reports to “Abram the Hebrew.” The parallel phrase מַמְרֵא הָאֱמֹרִי, “Mamre the Amorite,” likewise identifies a named man by his people.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute gentilic used in apposition to Abram.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69132:9, 66320:13.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a background clause. הוּא is an independent third-person masculine singular pronoun.

analysis.evidence: The pronoun הוּא refers to Abram, and בְּאֵלֹנֵי מַמְרֵא identifies where he was living when the fugitive brought him the news.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively with הוּא to describe Abram’s ongoing residence.
analysis.sense: dwell or live in a place

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69132:6, 68117:8.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state. The following name אַבְרָם supplies the possessor.
